title: GPT 6.2 Astra Pro: Specs, Benchmarks & Pricing
summary: GPT 6.2 Astra Pro launched November 17, 2026 with no production data yet. Decide whether integrating it into workflow automation now is worth the risks.
body_markdown:
## Compare GPT 6.2 Astra Pro cost and speed


Switching pays off only when a model's accuracy gain, or work your current model can't do, outweighs its cost per finished task. That cost isn't predictable from the price per token.


On OpenAI's[pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) , GPT-5 is listed at $10 per million output tokens, GPT-6 Astra at $50, and GPT-6.2 Astra at $40, so adopting an Astra model means paying **four to five times more per token** .


The flagship got five times dearer, then 20% cheaper, leaving it substantially more expensive than what it replaced, which means cost becomes a primary filter in adoption decisions. A budget approved on one release's wrong on the next.


The per-task figures move differently.[Reconscribe](https://reconscribe.com/gpt-6-2-astra/) measured one agent task at $8.99 on GPT-6 Astra and $2.89 on GPT-6.2 Astra.


That's about a third of the cost, even though the token price fell only a fifth, which means the newer model used far fewer tokens. Per-token price alone would have hidden that.


At $60.05 per task, Claude Fable 5.2 costs roughly twenty times GPT-6.2 Astra, according to the same source, so any large-scale application faces twenty-fold higher expenses with Fable. That's a defensible spend only if the task needs its long-horizon reasoning.


So compare on three numbers: cost per task, median time per task, and the failure rate you already track. Run your current model and the candidate over the same sample of real jobs.


Whoever gets paged when the workflow fails at 2am on a Tuesday also owns the bill, and should sign off on that comparison.
